ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2021-01-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Rodriguez, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Left flank pain and gross hematuria following high-speed motor vehicle collision

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Returning one year after left flank injury from a baseball bat, he presents to the emergency department following a motor vehicle collision. He was the restrained driver in a car that hit a tree at high speed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Suspected blunt renal trauma (left kidney) (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hypertension (diagnosed age 55)
- Mother: Hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Social, 1-2 drinks weekly. Occupation: Local delivery driver.

VITAL SIGNS:
Blood pressure of 130/85 mmHg, heart rate of 95 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 18 beats per minute

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, he is alert and oriented. His abdomen is soft with mild tenderness in the left flank, and there is a noticeable area of ecchymosis over the left costovertebral angle. No other injuries are noted.

LABORATORY DATA:
Urinalysis reveals red blood cells too numerous to count. His serum creatinine is 1.1 mg/dL, and hemoglobin is 13.2 g/dL.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Severe left flank pain after being struck by a baseball bat during neighborhood game, denies hematuria

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He presents to the emergency department after being struck on the left flank with a baseball bat during a neighborhood game. He complains of severe left flank pain but denies any hematuria, dysuria, or urgency.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
His past medical history is unremarkable

MEDICATIONS:
He takes no medications

ALLERGIES:
No known drug allergies

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: Hypertension (diagnosed age 55)
- Mother: Hypothyroidism

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Social, 1-2 drinks weekly. Occupation: Local delivery driver.

VITAL SIGNS:
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, heart rate is 98 beats per minute, and temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F)

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Abdominal examination reveals moderate tenderness to palpation over the left costovertebral angle without rebound or guarding. There is also a noticeable ecchymosis in the same area.

LABORATORY DATA:
Laboratory tests reveal the following:

- Hemoglobin: 13.8 g/dL
- White blood cell count: 7,500/mm³
- Platelets: 250,000/mm³
- Serum creatinine: 1.0 mg/dL
- Urinalysis: No red blood cells, no white blood cells, clear
